executiveFinding: The original requirements define ViceSharp as a C# derivative port whose observable behavior must match VICE x64sc at cycle-exact boundaries while retaining an independently designed .NET architecture. Git and MCP history also prove that May 2026 backfill work reused and overwrote the broad TR-CYCLE-001 identity with one narrow PAL frame-periodic behavior. That narrow behavior belongs under FR-VIC-001 acceptance coverage. No explicit rationale for the ID reuse was found, and requirements evidence alone does not prove that the overwrite caused later emulator implementation failures.

findings.claim: The earliest requirements set entered in the initial commit dated 2026-04-13.
findings.conclusion: The only root commit is d1f7175b70e0833ef9414faa98607130aa614da4, authored 2026-04-13T16:08:25-05:00. It created 31 files under docs/requirements with 4,230 inserted lines. The requirement documents themselves show Last Updated 2026-04-13.

findings.claim: ViceSharp was defined as a C# port and derivative work of VICE.
findings.conclusion: The initial README says both statements explicitly. Derivative work is stated in the licensing and attribution section and does not itself require internal line-for-line structure.

findings.claim: VICE x64sc was the accepted correctness reference and gold standard for cycle-accurate C64 behavior.
findings.conclusion: TR-CYCLE-001 explicitly calls x64sc the reference implementation for correctness and the accepted gold standard.

findings.claim: Required parity included cycle-by-cycle VIC-II DMA, passing VICE timing/test suites, and identical output for VICE cycle-exact programs.
findings.conclusion: The initial acceptance criteria require cycle-by-cycle DMA steal parity, 100 percent Lorenz parity with x64sc, identical output for VICE cycle-exact programs, and reference-capture comparison. FR-CPU-002 separately requires the CIA/VIC-II interleave to pass the VICE timing suite. FR-VIC-010 requires sprite DMA cycle positions to match x64sc.

findings.claim: The project was not required to copy VICE internals line-for-line because its original architecture requirements mandate a separate managed design.
findings.conclusion: This is a supported inference, not an explicit quote. The initial materials independently require a library-first .NET core, POCO state, UI-free reusable libraries, NativeAOT compatibility, fixed deterministic behavior, source generation, and thin UI consumers. Those constraints define ViceSharp's architecture while VICE defines behavioral reference outputs.
findings.qualification: No source contains the literal phrase 'do not copy VICE line-for-line'.

findings.claim: Hardware-confirmed behavior and independent hardware tests remain relevant, so VICE is an executable oracle but not the sole source of behavioral truth.
findings.conclusion: The original CPU requirement requires undocumented opcode behavior documented by the VICE team and confirmed by hardware testing. Other requirements require real-hardware timing and real-hardware comparison. Calling x64sc an executable oracle and not the sole source is an accurate synthesis.
commands: git grep -n -E 'confirmed by hardware|real hardware|hardware test|hardware timing' d1f7175b70e0833ef9414faa98607130aa614da4 -- docs/requirements

findings.claim: Current MCP createdAt values cannot establish original chronology because all 383 current records were imported together on 2026-09-28 and TR-CYCLE-001 has been repurposed.
findings.conclusion: Live MCP returned 140 FR, 127 TR, and 116 TEST records. Their createdAt values span 2026-09-28T18:12:16.1490511Z through 2026-09-28T18:12:41.0276658Z, 24.879 seconds. This is a bulk import timestamp window, not 2026-04 provenance. The current TR-CYCLE-001 body is the narrow PAL frame-periodic statement.
findings.qualification: The measured span is approximately 25 seconds, so 'roughly 20 seconds' is directionally correct but should be reported as 24.879 seconds for precision.

findings.claim: Original classification separates emulator behavior into FRs and the enabling clock/bus mechanism into TR-CYCLE-001.
findings.conclusion: FR-CPU-002 specifies opcode timing and CPU sub-cycle observability. FR-VIC-001 specifies PAL/NTSC raster behavior. FR-VIC-006 specifies badline and DMA stealing behavior. FR-VIC-010 specifies sprite DMA timing. TR-CYCLE-001 specifies PHI1/PHI2, bus arbitration, BA/AEC, per-cycle CPU pipeline, device tick granularity, and cross-device acceptance gates.

findings.claim: The May 2026 backfill/update overwrote the original broad TR-CYCLE-001 rather than adding a distinct scoped FR/TR.
findings.conclusion: The causal sequence is documented. On May 27, e73a820 exported TR-CYCLE-001 and FR-VIC-001 as placeholders backfilled from TODO links. On May 30, f608d02 added a narrow managed PAL frame-periodic test whose XML documentation cited the legacy FR-VIC-001 and TR-CYCLE-001 IDs. On May 31, the Claude session action explicitly says it updated 11 TRs including TR-CYCLE-001, and d1cbf30 replaced the full broad wiki body with the test's single narrow 19,656-cycle statement. The session's requirementsDiscovered list contains new TR-VIC edge and TEST IDs but not TR-CYCLE-001, corroborating update rather than creation.

findings.claim: There is an explicit recorded rationale explaining why the narrow behavior reused the original TR-CYCLE-001 ID.
findings.conclusion: No explicit rationale was found in the relevant commits, TODOs, generated documents, or persisted May 31 session turn. The evidence proves the mechanism and chronology but not the author's intent.
findings.likelyInference: The requirements update appears to have converted the test XML documentation into the requirement body while retaining IDs already used as traceability annotations. This is strongly suggested by near-identical wording, but it remains inference.
commands: git log --all -S 'Managed VIC-II CycleCounter advances by exactly 19,656' --format='%H %aI %s'

findings.claim: The current MCP state has concrete traceability and test-coverage gaps caused by the narrow replacement.
findings.conclusion: Current MCP has narrow closed FR-VIC-001 and TR-CYCLE-001 with zero acceptanceCriteria. FR-CPU-002 is absent. FR-VIC-006 and FR-VIC-010 are placeholders. The only relevant mappings connect narrow FR-VIC-001 or BACKFILL-VIDEO-001 to TR-CYCLE-001 and TEST-VIC-CHECKPOINT-001/TEST-VIC-RC-001. Those tests cover PAL frame periodicity, RC windows, read-only DMA, and one sprite checkpoint set, not the original broad CPU, CIA, PHI1/PHI2, BA/AEC, Lorenz, all-device, and cycle-exact-program acceptance surface.

findings.claim: The requirements overwrite directly caused later foundational emulator implementation failures.
findings.conclusion: The overwrite demonstrably removed broad requirement and test visibility from the current MCP projection, which can permit or conceal divergence. This review did not establish direct code-level causation between the record overwrite and any specific emulator defect. That requires separate implementation and regression-history evidence.
sourceAnchors: live MCP requirement and mapping state

findings.claim: The current MCP source of truth preserves the original broad TR-CYCLE-001 contract and its functional traceability.
findings.conclusion: It does not. Current MCP has the narrow frame-periodic body, while the current canonical markdown docs/requirements/technical/TR-Cycle-Accuracy.md still contains the original broad contract. The database and exported markdown projections are divergent, and the database currently lacks FR-CPU-002 while reducing FR-VIC-006/010 to placeholders.
